Commentary.Commentary: …THE RUN CHASE…

Chasing 122 for victory, India Women will fancy their chances of going 1–0 up in the series. Will the hosts wrap it up comfortably, or can Sri Lanka Women put up a fight with the ball? We’ll find out soon. Join us shortly for the second essay.

For India Women, the bowlers were outstanding and maintained pressure throughout the innings, but the fielding let them down with a few dropped catches in the outfield. Kranti Gaud, Deepti Sharma, and Sree Charani picked up a wicket each, while two run-outs also helped restrict Sri Lanka. Special mention to debutant Vaishnavi Sharma, who delivered an impressive and economical spell, conceding just four runs per over and keeping things tight.

A below-par batting performance from Sri Lanka Women saw them post a modest total of 121/6 from their 20 overs. After being asked to bat first, Chamari Athapaththu and Hasini Perera made decent starts but were unable to build on them. Vishmi Gunarathne top-scored with 39, though she struggled to find consistent timing and placement. Harshitha Samarawickrama contributed a useful 21 in the middle overs, while a brief cameo from Kaushini Nuthyangana helped Sri Lanka push past the 120-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: The pre-match formalities are complete, and all set for the action to begin! The teams and umpires are making their way onto the field. Opening the innings for Sri Lanka Women are Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunarathne, while Kranti Gaud will start with the ball for India Women. Let's play...
The teams and match officials have lined up for the national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's anthem first, followed by that of India. Live action is coming shortly.

Pitch Report - WV Raman and Anjum Chopra are at the pitchside. WV Raman comments that the conditions are fantastic on a cool evening. He notes that the straight boundaries measure 68 meters, while the square boundaries are 59 meters and 50 meters. Anjum Chopra adds that it is a beautiful track to bat on. She mentions that for any player looking to make a comeback after being out of form, this is the ideal surface. The pitch is nicely rolled and expected to be high-scoring, which means bowlers will need to be precise and disciplined. She also highlights that both teams might consider having an extra seam bowling option if they choose to bowl first. WV Raman concludes by pointing out that there is likely to be dew later in the day, which could influence conditions.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Chamari Athapaththu(C), Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Vishmi Gunarathne, Kaushini Nuthyangana(WK), Inoka Ranaweera, Malki Madara, Kawya Kavindi, Shashini Gimhani.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur(C), Richa Ghosh(WK), Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur, Arundhati Reddy, Vaishnavi Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Sree Charani.

Chamari Athapaththu, the Sri Lanka Women's captain, says they had good preparation and hopes to have a strong game today. She adds that the board and selectors have decided to give opportunities to young players and hopes they play their best cricket. She concludes by saying they have a good team and need to stick to their plans.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the Indian Women’s skipper, won the toss and opted to bowl first. She mentioned that dew is expected to play a significant role, which is why they have gone with three pacers today, hoping to make the most of the conditions. She also revealed that Vaishnavi Sharma is making her debut. Calling it a new series and format for the team, Harmanpreet said they are focused on enjoying the challenge. She concluded by saying that the side wants to play fearless cricket and bring plenty of energy to the field.
TOSS - India Women have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

It promises to be a fascinating contest between India’s established power-hitters and Sri Lanka’s energetic young brigade. With India looking to dominate at home and Sri Lanka aiming for an upset, we are in for a thrilling start to the series. Sit back and enjoy the action! Toss and team news in a bit...

On the other side, Sri Lanka is fielding a youthful side led by the experienced Chamari Athapaththu. The visitors have rested several seniors to back young talent, including the ambidextrous teenage spinning sensation, Shashini Gimhani. With reliable batters like Harshitha Samarawickrama and the dynamic all-rounder Kavisha Dilhari, Sri Lanka will be keen to challenge the hosts.

Captain Harmanpreet Kaur leads a confident squad that remains largely similar to the World Cup-winning team, with Smriti Mandhana serving as her deputy. Fans will be eager to see Shafali Verma opening the batting after her heroics in the recent final. There is also fresh excitement in the air with maiden call-ups for 19-year-old Vaishnavi Sharma and wicketkeeper G Kamalini, alongside the return of pacer Renuka Singh Thakur.

The wait is over! The newly crowned ODI World Cup champions, India Women, are back in action today as they take on Sri Lanka Women in the first T20I of the five-match series. The stage is set at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam, where the Women in Blue will look to carry their winning momentum into the shortest format of the game.
... MATCH DAY ...

The calendar flips to 2026 in a few weeks, and with it comes the Women’s T20 World Cup in England and Wales, all set for June-July. Preparations don’t start a month before a World Cup, they start now. India Women face Sri Lanka Women in the first of the two T20Is scheduled for Visakhapatnam, followed by the next three in Thiruvananthapuram. India arrive as freshly crowned ODI World Champions after their historic triumph in November. The tag feels good, but it also brings weight. Expectations have skyrocketed. The pressure to dominate across formats has multiplied. Sri Lanka haven’t toured India for a bilateral T20I series since 2016, when India won 3-0 . Nearly a decade since their last visit. That’s a massive gap. Much has changed in women’s cricket since then - more professionalism, better infrastructure, higher standards. India lead the head-to-head comfortably with 20 wins from 26 meetings , but history only matters if you let it affect you. Sri Lanka won’t. Let’s talk about India first. Harmanpreet Kaur leads with Smriti Mandhana as her deputy . Two experienced heads who’ve seen everything the game can throw at them. Deepti Sharma was Player of the Tournament at the ODI World Cup, while Shafali Verma starred as Player of the Match in the final. Both are riding confidence, both want more success. That hunger matters. Smriti Mandhana remains the key. When she’s in form, she makes batting look ridiculously easy. She has scored the most number of runs in the shortest format this calendar year and the only one to score a century. Jemimah Rodrigues brings stability through the middle overs, capable of anchoring or accelerating depending on the situation. Harmanpreet herself can finish games with brutal efficiency, while Richa Ghosh needs no introduction down the order. She has the knack of finishing games in style and has does so with conviction. But here’s what makes this series interesting - two teenagers, Kamalini G and Vaishnavi Sharma, have earned maiden call-ups. Kamalini is just 17, a wicketkeeper-batter who’s already played in the Women’s Premier League. Vaishnavi was India’s leading wicket-taker at the recent U-19 Women’s Cricket World Cup . Fresh blood. Young talent getting opportunities. India’s strength is obvious - batting depth that goes seven or eight down, quality spin options in Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana, and Sree Charani, who has impressed with her craft sincerely. Renuka Singh Thakur returns after injury kept her out of the England series. Her swing bowling with the new ball makes her a handy bowler. And now, Sri Lanka. Chamari Athapaththu leads a side that knows the odds are stacked against them. The squad is young, relatively inexperienced, and in transition. Sri Lankan cricket faces a familiar challenge - they’ve leaned heavily on Athapaththu for years, and now they’re searching for the next generation to share the load. Athapaththu herself remains world-class. An all-rounder who can dismantle attacks with the bat and deliver crucial overs with the ball. When she’s in form, she’s unstoppable. But that’s the problem - Sri Lanka can’t rely on one player to carry them through five matches. They need others stepping up consistently. Samarawickrama has shown improvement and provides middle-order stability. Nilakshika Silva brings experience to the batting lineup. But consistency remains the issue. The bowling has depth in spin. Inoka Ranaweera, Shashini Gimhani, and Kavisha Dilhari lead the spin attack, with Athapaththu chipping in when needed. That’s plenty of variety and control through the middle overs. The pace department includes Malki Madara, Malsha Shehani, and Kavya Kavindi. Without genuine express pace though, they’ll need to be smart with variations. Sri Lanka Women have played just three T20Is this year so it will be a big challenge against a spirited Indian side, bouyed by their recent World Cup triumph. Promises to be a cracker.
